name: quicklinks
title: Quicklinks
description: Your own links, with a {query} placeholder for search URLs: open one, fill it in, or copy it. Created and edited in the panel (a browser to open with, the url filled from the tab in front), a library of ready-made searches, imported and exported as JSON.
author: pal

settings.label: Prefer an open tab
settings.text: Open a link by switching to a browser tab already on that page, when there is one
settings.description: Asks the browsers (as Browser Tabs does) before opening; a new tab when none has the page.

store.tagline: Your own links, with a {query} slot for search URLs
features: Enter opens the link; one with `{query}` in its url (`https://github.com/search?q={query}`) takes it as a typed argument in the search bar (one field per placeholder name), percent-encoded

`{selection}`, `{clipboard}` and `{files}` in a url are filled without asking (the text selected in the app in front, the newest copy, the paths selected in Finder), so `https://translate.google.com/?text={selection}` opens in one Enter

Create Quicklink is a form (name, url, keywords, the browser to open with), its url and name filled from the tab in front; Edit (`cmd+e`) opens it filled in, a url with no scheme is refused under the field
Browse Library: 25 ready-made searches (Google, Wikipedia, GitHub, npm, MDN, Stack Overflow, Maps...) added to your links with Enter, or searched with at once (`cmd+enter`)
Keywords are extra words the search matches; the placeholder shows as a tag, the favicon comes from the site
`prefer_existing_tab`: a link whose page is open in a browser tab switches to that tab instead of opening another
Raycast's `{argument}` and `{argument name="Repo"}` are read the same way as `{query}`
Import Quicklinks and Export Quicklinks move the list as a JSON array of `{name, url, keywords?, app?}` (Raycast's export is read too)
An `import` file adds read-only links next to your own, read on every listing
